text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Friday.

GERMANY - A U.S. bond rally infected the German market, sending prices higher in afternoon trading and setting the stage for still more gains next week. The March Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 102.56, up 0.45 from Thursday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - Gilts inched back from a new all-time high set earlier on Friday, but still ended the session more than a full point higher on the day. The March long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 113-06/32, up 1-01/32 from Thursday's settlement price.

FRANCE - Bonds ended the week with a sparkle as market-positive U.S. employment data pushed 10-year OAT yields to their lowest levels in decades and shunted the March future to a contract high. The March notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 131.28, up 0.38 from Thursday's settlement price.

ITALY - Debt markets climbed amid a positive bond market environment, with Btp futures ending up near the day's highs. The March bond future on LIFFE was trading at 131.40, up 1.06 from Thursday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasury prices opened firm as players awaited the January employment report. The March Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 112-20/32, up 20/32 from Thursday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.7 percent.

JAPAN - Key March Japanese government bond futures ended the Tokyo session higher following a fall in Tokyo stocks. In after hours trading the March future on LIFFE was trading at 126.53, up 0.27 from Thursday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - The Eurobond market was subdued as the markets focused on January U.S. employment data. Non-farm payrolls rose by more than expected but this was offset by a fall in hours worked and a rise in the unemployment rate, so bond markets rose. In the pipeline for next week is a jumbo three-tranche euro Eurobond for Siemens which will total up to 2.0 billion marks equivalent. Panama will launch a $500 million five-year bond and Colombia plans a $750 million 10-year deal.
